title: Our Screen Together: A Bridge for Conversation, Not a Silent Wall
summary:
Imagine your little one, with wide eyes, staring at the screen. They might seem quiet and engrossed, which gives you a few moments of peace. But have you ever wondered what’s going on in their mind? Are they just a passive recipient, or is there a way to transform this time into a real opportunity for growth and connection? We often resort to the screen as a 'silent babysitter,' but the truth is that every minute a child spends in front of it alone can be a lost opportunity to enhance their language and interaction.

The secret lies in 'shared viewing.' Not every screen minute is equal. When you sit next to your child, comment on what they see, name objects, and ask simple questions, you transform screen time from a one-way broadcast into a lively, two-way dialogue. This participation not only reduces the potential negative effects of screen time but also significantly multiplies its benefits, turning digital content into a linguistic and interactive tool that enriches their small world.

Start by choosing calm, slow-paced content appropriate for their age, then sit with them. Comment on what’s happening: “Look! The rabbit is jumping high!” And connect it to their reality: “Remember our red ball? This ball looks like it!” By doing this, the screen becomes a bridge connecting their digital world with their real world, teaching them how to be interactive and engaged, not just a passive recipient. It’s a golden opportunity to strengthen your bond and develop their language and social skills in a fun and warm way.
try_this: Tonight: Sit with your child while they watch the screen (even if only for a few minutes), comment on one thing they see, then link it to something familiar in your home (like a toy or a pet).
